+# Hanna's Quadrupled Linear Rows and Dyadic Parity
+
+## Abstract
+
+An integer source series exists for OEIS A397594, and every source series has Hanna's dyadic-neighbor odd support.
+
+The ordinary formal series has a(n)=PowerSeries.coeff n A, with index zero and a(0)=1. Rational rescaling substitutes X/m after mapping each integer coefficient to Q. All powers are formal-series products. Subtraction between natural indices is truncated natural subtraction; no analytic convergence is required.
+
+**Definition 1.1 (The rational-rescaling source equation).**
+
+$$\forall A \in \operatorname{PowerSeries}\left(\mathbb{Z}\right),\; \operatorname{IsSourceSeries}\left(A\right) \Leftrightarrow ((\operatorname{PowerSeries}.\operatorname{constantCoeff}\left(A\right) = 1) \land (\forall m \in \mathbb{N},\; (0 < m) \Rightarrow (\sum_{j \in \operatorname{Finset}.\operatorname{range}\left(m\right)} \operatorname{PowerSeries}.\operatorname{coeff}\left(j, (\operatorname{PowerSeries}.\operatorname{rescale}\left((m: \mathbb{Q})^{-1}, \operatorname{PowerSeries}.\operatorname{map}\left(\operatorname{Int}.\operatorname{castRingHom}\left(\mathbb{Q}\right), A\right)\right))^{m}\right) = (4: \mathbb{Q})^{m - 1})))$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S1/Recurrence/LinearRows/QuadrupledLinearExponentDyadicSupport.IsSourceSeries` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* Paul D. Hanna (2026). *OEIS A397594: quadrupled linear rows and dyadic parity*. URL: <https://oeis.org/A397594>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+OEIS A397594 revision 15, NAME and FORMULA (1), without pagination: "G.f. A(x) such that the sum of the first n coefficients in A(x/n)^n equals 4^(n-1) for n >= 1." "(1) 4^(n-1) = Sum_{k=0..n-1} [x^k] A(x/n)^n for n >= 1." The natural m below is the source's n, and j is its k. Finset.range m contains exactly j=0 through m-1. The equation is in Q, with A in PowerSeries Z and constant coefficient one.
+
+**Definition 1.2 (Integer existence and the parity assertion).**
+
+$$claim \Leftrightarrow ((\exists A \in \operatorname{PowerSeries}\left(\mathbb{Z}\right),\; \operatorname{IsSourceSeries}\left(A\right)) \land (\forall A \in \operatorname{PowerSeries}\left(\mathbb{Z}\right),\; (\operatorname{IsSourceSeries}\left(A\right)) \Rightarrow (\forall n \in \mathbb{N},\; (3 < n) \Rightarrow (\operatorname{Odd}\left(\operatorname{PowerSeries}.\operatorname{coeff}\left(n, A\right)\right) \Leftrightarrow (\exists k \in \mathbb{N},\; (1 < k) \land (n = 2^{k} - 1 \lor n = 2^{k} + 1))))))$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S1/Recurrence/LinearRows/QuadrupledLinearExponentDyadicSupport.claim` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* Paul D. Hanna (2026). *OEIS A397594: quadrupled linear rows and dyadic parity*. URL: <https://oeis.org/A397594>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+OEIS A397594 revision 15, COMMENTS, without pagination: "Conjecture: for n > 3, a(n) is odd iff n is of the form 2^k-1 or 2^k+1 (k > 1)." Here a(n)=PowerSeries.coeff n A, n and k are natural numbers, and Odd applies to an integer coefficient. Existence of an integer source series is included, and the equivalence quantifies over every source series.
+
+**Theorem 1.3 (Hanna's parity assertion proved).**
+
+$$(\exists A \in \operatorname{PowerSeries}\left(\mathbb{Z}\right),\; \operatorname{IsSourceSeries}\left(A\right)) \land (\forall A \in \operatorname{PowerSeries}\left(\mathbb{Z}\right),\; (\operatorname{IsSourceSeries}\left(A\right)) \Rightarrow (\forall n \in \mathbb{N},\; (3 < n) \Rightarrow (\operatorname{Odd}\left(\operatorname{PowerSeries}.\operatorname{coeff}\left(n, A\right)\right) \Leftrightarrow (\exists k \in \mathbb{N},\; (1 < k) \land (n = 2^{k} - 1 \lor n = 2^{k} + 1)))))$$
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S1/Recurrence/LinearRows/QuadrupledLinearExponentDyadicSupport.result` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Resolves.* `Problems/hanna397594` (proved) by `D5/S1/Recurrence/LinearRows/QuadrupledLinearExponentDyadicSupport.result`.
+
+<!-- scribe-open-problem-resolution-v1 {"problem_slug":"hanna397594","declaration_gid":"D5/S1/Recurrence/LinearRows/QuadrupledLinearExponentDyadicSupport.result","resolution_kind":"proved"} -->
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Paul D. Hanna (2026). *OEIS A397594: quadrupled linear rows and dyadic parity*. URL: <https://oeis.org/A397594>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Clearing the rescaling denominators gives the integer row equation. Triangular normalization has forcing 4^n(n+1)^(n-1) in positive degree. Coefficientwise iteration constructs an integer solution. The forcing vanishes modulo two, so normalized uniqueness and the homogeneous dyadic-support theorem give the parity equivalence for every source solution. The assertion concerns the parameter four; the entire parameter triangle and the source's reversion identities are separate questions.
+

+    private static Formula SourceDefinition()
+    {
+        var a = F.Id("A");
+        var m = F.Id("m");
+        var j = F.Id("j");
+        var rationalMap = Call(Qualified("Int", "castRingHom"), Rationals());
+        var rationalImage = Call(Qualified("PowerSeries", "map"), rationalMap, a);
+        var inverse = new Formula.Power(Cast(m, Rationals()), Seq(Minus, D(1)));
+        var scaled = Call(Qualified("PowerSeries", "rescale"), inverse, rationalImage);
+        var sum = Seq(new Formula.Subscript(Sum,
+            new Formula.Relation(j, FormulaRelationOperator.MemberOf,
+                Call(Qualified("Finset", "range"), m))), Sp,
+            Coeff(j, new Formula.Power(Parenthesized(scaled), m)));
+        var rows = All("m", Naturals(), ImpliesFormula(Less(D(0), m),
+            Equal(sum, new Formula.Power(Cast(D(4), Rationals()), Sub(m, D(1))))));
+        var body = And(Equal(Call(Qualified("PowerSeries", "constantCoeff"), a), D(1)), rows);
+        return Disp(All("A", SeriesType(), new Formula.Logic(
+            SourceAt(a), FormulaLogicOperator.Iff, Parenthesized(body))));
+    }
+
+    private static Formula ClaimBody()
+    {
+        var a = F.Id("A");
+        var n = F.Id("n");
+        var k = F.Id("k");
+        var power = new Formula.Power(D(2), k);
+        var support = ExistsFormula("k", Naturals(), And(Less(D(1), k),
+            new Formula.Logic(Equal(n, Sub(power, D(1))), FormulaLogicOperator.Or,
+                Equal(n, Add(power, D(1))))));
+        var parity = All("A", SeriesType(), ImpliesFormula(SourceAt(a),
+            All("n", Naturals(), ImpliesFormula(Less(D(3), n),
+                new Formula.Logic(Call("Odd", Coeff(n, a)), FormulaLogicOperator.Iff,
+                    Parenthesized(support))))));
+        return And(ExistsFormula("A", SeriesType(), SourceAt(a)), parity);
+    }
+
+    private static Formula SourceAt(Formula a) => Call("IsSourceSeries", a);
+    private static Formula Coeff(Formula n, Formula a) => Call(Qualified("PowerSeries", "coeff"), n, a);
+    private static Formula SeriesType() => Call("PowerSeries", Seq(Mathbb, Grp(F.Id("Z"))));
+    private static Formula Naturals() => Seq(Mathbb, Grp(F.Id("N")));
+    private static Formula Rationals() => Seq(Mathbb, Grp(F.Id("Q")));
+    private static Formula Qualified(string owner, string name) =>
+        Seq(Operatorname, Grp(F.Id(owner)), Dot, Operatorname, Grp(F.Id(name)));
+    private static Formula Call(string name, params Formula[] args) =>
+        new Formula.FunctionCall(FormulaIdentifier.Create(name), [.. args]);
+    private static Formula Call(Formula function, params Formula[] args) => new Formula.Apply(function, [.. args]);
+    private static Formula Cast(Formula value, Formula type) => Parenthesized(Seq(value, Colon, Sp, type));
+    private static Formula Add(Formula left, Formula right) => new Formula.Binary(left, FormulaBinaryOperator.Add, right);
+    private static Formula Sub(Formula left, Formula right) => new Formula.Binary(left, FormulaBinaryOperator.Subtract, right);
+    private static Formula Equal(Formula left, Formula right) => new Formula.Relation(left, FormulaRelationOperator.Equal, right);
+    private static Formula Less(Formula left, Formula right) => new Formula.Relation(left, FormulaRelationOperator.LessThan, right);
+    private static Formula And(Formula left, Formula right) =>
+        new Formula.Logic(Parenthesized(left), FormulaLogicOperator.And, Parenthesized(right));
+    private static Formula ImpliesFormula(Formula left, Formula right) =>
+        new Formula.Logic(Parenthesized(left), FormulaLogicOperator.Implies, Parenthesized(right));
+    private static Formula All(string name, Formula type, Formula body) =>
+        new Formula.Bind(FormulaQuantifier.ForAll, FormulaIdentifier.Create(name), type, body);
+    private static Formula ExistsFormula(string name, Formula type, Formula body) =>
+        new Formula.Bind(FormulaQuantifier.Exists, FormulaIdentifier.Create(name), type, body);
+    private static Formula Parenthesized(Formula value) => Seq(Open, value, Close);
+}

+# Masks, reached sets and original coordinate reconstruction
+
+## Abstract
+
+Native masks recover complete original row exteriors
+
+**Theorem 1.1 (Complete exterior descriptors and all original rows have one exact image).**
+
+$$\forall X: Type, (\forall p: \operatorname{Presentation}\left(X\right), (\forall d: Nat, (\forall pat: \operatorname{Pattern}\left(d\right), (\forall name: \operatorname{Frontier}\left(pat\right) \to X, (\forall rs: \operatorname{List}\left(RawRow\right), (\forall extra: \operatorname{SignedConstraints}\left(X\right), (\forall v: X \to Source, ((\forall r: RawRow, ((r \in rs) \implies (\operatorname{CutPrefixFree}\left(\operatorname{fst}\left(r\right)\right)))) \implies ((\forall r: RawRow, ((r \in rs) \implies (\forall q: Address, ((q \in \operatorname{fst}\left(r\right)) \implies (\operatorname{length}\left(q\right) < d))))) \implies ((\forall Q: CutSet, (\forall u: Source, (\forall w: Source, (((\operatorname{nativeMask}\left(Q, \operatorname{nil}\left(\right), u\right) = \operatorname{nativeMask}\left(Q, \operatorname{nil}\left(\right), w\right)) \land (\operatorname{toFinset}\left(\operatorname{reachedHoles}\left(Q, \operatorname{nil}\left(\right), u\right)\right) = \operatorname{toFinset}\left(\operatorname{reachedHoles}\left(Q, \operatorname{nil}\left(\right), w\right)\right))) \iff (\operatorname{cutExterior}\left(Q, \operatorname{nil}\left(\right), u\right) = \operatorname{cutExterior}\left(Q, \operatorname{nil}\left(\right), w\right)))))) \land ((\forall r: RawRow, ((r \in rs) \implies (\operatorname{evaluate}\left(v, \operatorname{maskExpression}\left(\operatorname{symbolicExterior}\left(\operatorname{fst}\left(r\right), \operatorname{nil}\left(\right), \operatorname{patternTerm}\left(pat, name\right)\right)\right)\right) = \operatorname{nativeMask}\left(\operatorname{fst}\left(r\right), \operatorname{nil}\left(\right), \operatorname{fill}\left(pat, \operatorname{composition}\left(v, name\right)\right)\right)))) \land (((\forall r: RawRow, ((r \in rs) \implies (\operatorname{maskRowHolds}\left(r, \operatorname{fill}\left(pat, \operatorname{composition}\left(v, name\right)\right)\right)))) \land ((\forall e: \operatorname{Prod}\left(\operatorname{Term}\left(X\right), \operatorname{Term}\left(X\right)\right), ((e \in \operatorname{fst}\left(extra\right)) \implies (\operatorname{evaluate}\left(v, \operatorname{fst}\left(e\right)\right) = \operatorname{evaluate}\left(v, \operatorname{snd}\left(e\right)\right)))) \land (\forall e: \operatorname{Prod}\left(\operatorname{Term}\left(X\right), \operatorname{Term}\left(X\right)\right), ((e \in \operatorname{snd}\left(extra\right)) \implies (\operatorname{evaluate}\left(v, \operatorname{fst}\left(e\right)\right) \neq \operatorname{evaluate}\left(v, \operatorname{snd}\left(e\right)\right)))))) \iff (\exists o: \operatorname{RowOutput}\left(X\right), ((\operatorname{eliminateRows}\left(p, \operatorname{patternTerm}\left(pat, name\right), rs, extra\right) = \operatorname{some}\left(o\right)) \land (\exists z: \operatorname{free}\left(o\right) \to Source, ((\forall x: X, (\operatorname{evaluate}\left(z, \operatorname{theta}\left(o, x\right)\right) = \operatorname{v}\left(x\right))) \land (\forall e: \operatorname{Prod}\left(\operatorname{Term}\left(\operatorname{free}\left(o\right)\right), \operatorname{Term}\left(\operatorname{free}\left(o\right)\right)\right), ((e \in \operatorname{delta}\left(o\right)) \implies (\operatorname{evaluate}\left(z, \operatorname{fst}\left(e\right)\right) \neq \operatorname{evaluate}\left(z, \operatorname{snd}\left(e\right)\right))))))))))))))))))))$$
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Observer/Constructor/NativeMaskRowElimination.original_mask_row_elimination` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+The native mask recursively replaces each encountered cut subtree by alpha, the Boolean leaf true. A concrete exterior instead replaces it by its literal address hole. Filling every address hole by alpha gives exactly the native mask. Cutting that filled mask again at the original cuts restores the complete exterior. Thus equality of masks together with equality of reached sets is equivalent to equality of complete exteriors on the original tree carrier. Concrete leaves and ordered branches outside the cuts are retained without a size bound.
+
+For an arbitrary raw row, maskRowHolds means the following conjunction: cutting the label's filled mask at its cut set gives back its literal exterior; the source mask equals that filled mask; the source reached set equals the set of literal address holes; and the entire actual partition equals the label relation. The first conjunct checks address coherence directly. It is automatic for an exterior cut from any source, and rejects malformed raw labels without an attained-label certificate. The other three conjuncts retain both complete exterior descriptors and every partition bit.
+
+Every row is evaluated on the same original source fill(pat,composition(v,name)). The maskExpression operation changes literal address holes to alpha in the symbolic exterior and retains every uncut frontier variable. The second conjunct identifies evaluation of this native term with the concrete mask of that very original source. Each row cut is prefix-free and every cut address has length strictly less than d. The list may contain both old and new cuts and any additional rows. The source has its actual original prefix pattern and the same named frontiers throughout; the identity naming map retains every original frontier coordinate. Early ground leaves, absent cuts, the root cut, uncut frontiers and repeated names remain in scope.
+
+All reached ordered pairs are retained by the underlying row compiler, including diagonals, both orders, repeated classes and all cross-class and off-task disequalities. An empty reached set has no pairs. A one-hole partition has no distinct pair tests; its ordered diagonal is the reflexive equality, and a raw label denying that equality has empty solution domain. No selected partition projection replaces the complete relation.
+
+The same finite extra equations and disequalities enter the existing full row elimination. The output has an explicitly enumerated free subtype of the original finite presentation, a total substitution theta for every original coordinate, and only substituted disequalities delta. One unrestricted valuation z on that free subtype reconstructs every original coordinate, including unused variables and auxiliaries. Replacing all original coordinates in the pattern term therefore reconstructs the same original source. Interpreted substitution histories, mixed image construction, and all-rank cofinality require further results.
+

+

+    private static Formula V(string s) => F.Id(s);

+    private static Formula Imp(Formula a, Formula b) => Seq(Par(a), Sp, Implies, Sp, Par(b));
+    private static Formula Arr(Formula a, Formula b) => Seq(a, Sp, To, Sp, b);
+    private static Formula Fst(Formula a) => C("fst", a);
+    private static Formula Snd(Formula a) => C("snd", a);
+    private static Formula Bounded(string x, Formula type, Formula list, Formula body) =>
+        All(x, type, Imp(Seq(V(x), Sp, InMacro, Sp, list), body));
+
+    private static Formula Exterior()
+    {
+        var q = V("Q");
+        var u = V("u");
+        var w = V("w");
+        return All("Q", V("CutSet"), All("u", V("Source"), All("w", V("Source"),
+            IffOf(And(
+                EqOf(C("nativeMask", q, C("nil"), u), C("nativeMask", q, C("nil"), w)),
+                EqOf(C("toFinset", C("reachedHoles", q, C("nil"), u)),
+                    C("toFinset", C("reachedHoles", q, C("nil"), w)))),
+                EqOf(C("cutExterior", q, C("nil"), u), C("cutExterior", q, C("nil"), w))))));
+    }
+
+    private static Formula Extras()
+    {
+        var pair = C("Prod", C("Term", V("X")), C("Term", V("X")));
+        var e = V("e");
+        return And(
+            Bounded("e", pair, Fst(V("extra")), EqOf(C("evaluate", V("v"), Fst(e)), C("evaluate", V("v"), Snd(e)))),
+            Bounded("e", pair, Snd(V("extra")), Seq(C("evaluate", V("v"), Fst(e)), Sp, Neq, Sp, C("evaluate", V("v"), Snd(e)))));
+    }
+
+    private static Formula Image()
+    {
+        var o = V("o");
+        var z = V("z");
+        var e = V("e");
+        var free = C("free", o);
+        var reconstructed = All("x", V("X"), EqOf(C("evaluate", z, C("theta", o, V("x"))), C("v", V("x"))));
+        var negatives = Bounded("e", C("Prod", C("Term", free), C("Term", free)), C("delta", o),
+            Seq(C("evaluate", z, Fst(e)), Sp, Neq, Sp, C("evaluate", z, Snd(e))));
+        return Some("o", C("RowOutput", V("X")),
+            And(EqOf(C("eliminateRows", V("p"), C("patternTerm", V("pat"), V("name")), V("rs"), V("extra")), C("some", o)),
+                Some("z", Arr(free, V("Source")), And(reconstructed, negatives))));
+    }
+
+    private static Formula Statement()
+    {
+        var r = V("r");
+        var rs = V("rs");
+        var source = C("fill", V("pat"), C("composition", V("v"), V("name")));
+        var rows = Bounded("r", V("RawRow"), rs, C("maskRowHolds", r, source));
+        var expressions = Bounded("r", V("RawRow"), rs,
+            EqOf(C("evaluate", V("v"), C("maskExpression", C("symbolicExterior", Fst(r), C("nil"), C("patternTerm", V("pat"), V("name"))))),
+                C("nativeMask", Fst(r), C("nil"), source)));
+        var prefix = Bounded("r", V("RawRow"), rs, C("CutPrefixFree", Fst(r)));
+        var depth = Bounded("r", V("RawRow"), rs,
+            Bounded("q", V("Address"), Fst(r), Seq(C("length", V("q")), Sp, Lt, Sp, V("d"))));
+        Formula body = Imp(prefix, Imp(depth,
+            And(Exterior(), And(expressions, IffOf(And(rows, Extras()), Image())))));
+        body = All("v", Arr(V("X"), V("Source")), body);
+        body = All("extra", C("SignedConstraints", V("X")), body);
+        body = All("rs", C("List", V("RawRow")), body);
+        body = All("name", Arr(C("Frontier", V("pat")), V("X")), body);
+        body = All("pat", C("Pattern", V("d")), body);
+        body = All("d", V("Nat"), body);
+        body = All("p", C("Presentation", V("X")), body);
+        return All("X", V("Type"), body);
+    }
+}

+# Complete raw rows and shared source reconstruction
+
+## Abstract
+
+Complete raw row elimination over one original variable family
+
+**Theorem 1.1 (A symbolic exterior matches exactly when its finite bindings hold).**
+
+$$\forall X: Type, (\forall p: \operatorname{SymbolicExterior}\left(X\right), (\forall u: HoleExterior, (\forall v: X \to Source, ((\operatorname{exteriorFill}\left(v, p\right) = u) \iff (\exists bs: \operatorname{List}\left(\operatorname{Prod}\left(X, \operatorname{Term}\left(X\right)\right)\right), ((\operatorname{matchExterior}\left(p, u\right) = \operatorname{some}\left(bs\right)) \land (\operatorname{bindingHolds}\left(v, bs\right))))))))$$
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Observer/Constructor/NativeSymbolicRowElimination.exterior_match_exact` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+A symbolic exterior has Boolean leaves, residual variables and literal address holes. The matcher descends through ordered pair constructors, rejects constructor and hole mismatches, and decodes a target subtree into a source term only when that subtree contains no address hole. Every successful variable match contributes an explicit binding to a finite list; repeated variables are retained as repeated bindings.
+
+For every valuation, the theorem equates the filled symbolic exterior with an arbitrary concrete hole exterior exactly with the existence of the matcher output whose bindings all evaluate to the valuation. Constructor and address-hole mismatches are rejected. Literal holes with the same address match exactly, while residual variables expand only to hole-free source subtrees and retain every returned binding. The full row compiler combines these bindings with every sign of the reached partition. Interpreted positive history equations remain separate.
+
+**Theorem 1.2 (All raw rows and free signed comparisons share one exact reconstruction).**
+
+$$\forall X: Type, (\forall p: \operatorname{Presentation}\left(X\right), (\forall t: \operatorname{Term}\left(X\right), (\forall rs: \operatorname{List}\left(RawRow\right), (\forall extra: \operatorname{SignedConstraints}\left(X\right), (\forall v: X \to Source, ((((\forall r: RawRow, ((r \in rs) \implies (\operatorname{symbolicRecord}\left(\operatorname{fst}\left(r\right), t, v\right) = \operatorname{snd}\left(r\right)))) \land ((\forall c: \operatorname{Prod}\left(\operatorname{Term}\left(X\right), \operatorname{Term}\left(X\right)\right), ((c \in \operatorname{fst}\left(extra\right)) \implies (\operatorname{evaluate}\left(v, \operatorname{fst}\left(c\right)\right) = \operatorname{evaluate}\left(v, \operatorname{snd}\left(c\right)\right)))) \land (\forall e: \operatorname{Prod}\left(\operatorname{Term}\left(X\right), \operatorname{Term}\left(X\right)\right), ((e \in \operatorname{snd}\left(extra\right)) \implies (\operatorname{evaluate}\left(v, \operatorname{fst}\left(e\right)\right) \neq \operatorname{evaluate}\left(v, \operatorname{snd}\left(e\right)\right)))))) \iff (\exists o: \operatorname{RowOutput}\left(X\right), ((\operatorname{eliminateRows}\left(p, t, rs, extra\right) = \operatorname{some}\left(o\right)) \land (\exists z: \operatorname{free}\left(o\right) \to Source, ((\forall x: X, (\operatorname{evaluate}\left(z, \operatorname{theta}\left(o, x\right)\right) = \operatorname{v}\left(x\right))) \land (\forall e: \operatorname{Prod}\left(\operatorname{Term}\left(\operatorname{free}\left(o\right)\right), \operatorname{Term}\left(\operatorname{free}\left(o\right)\right)\right), ((e \in \operatorname{delta}\left(o\right)) \implies (\operatorname{evaluate}\left(z, \operatorname{fst}\left(e\right)\right) \neq \operatorname{evaluate}\left(z, \operatorname{snd}\left(e\right)\right))))))))) \land (\forall d: Nat, (\forall pat: \operatorname{Pattern}\left(d\right), (\forall name: \operatorname{Frontier}\left(pat\right) \to X, ((t = \operatorname{patternTerm}\left(pat, name\right)) \implies ((\forall r: RawRow, ((r \in rs) \implies (\operatorname{CutPrefixFree}\left(\operatorname{fst}\left(r\right)\right)))) \implies ((\forall r: RawRow, ((r \in rs) \implies (\forall q: Address, ((q \in \operatorname{fst}\left(r\right)) \implies (\operatorname{length}\left(q\right) < d))))) \implies (((\forall r: RawRow, ((r \in rs) \implies (\operatorname{literalRecord}\left(\operatorname{fst}\left(r\right), \operatorname{fill}\left(pat, \operatorname{composition}\left(v, name\right)\right)\right) = \operatorname{snd}\left(r\right)))) \land ((\forall c: \operatorname{Prod}\left(\operatorname{Term}\left(X\right), \operatorname{Term}\left(X\right)\right), ((c \in \operatorname{fst}\left(extra\right)) \implies (\operatorname{evaluate}\left(v, \operatorname{fst}\left(c\right)\right) = \operatorname{evaluate}\left(v, \operatorname{snd}\left(c\right)\right)))) \land (\forall e: \operatorname{Prod}\left(\operatorname{Term}\left(X\right), \operatorname{Term}\left(X\right)\right), ((e \in \operatorname{snd}\left(extra\right)) \implies (\operatorname{evaluate}\left(v, \operatorname{fst}\left(e\right)\right) \neq \operatorname{evaluate}\left(v, \operatorname{snd}\left(e\right)\right)))))) \iff (\exists o: \operatorname{RowOutput}\left(X\right), ((\operatorname{eliminateRows}\left(p, t, rs, extra\right) = \operatorname{some}\left(o\right)) \land (\exists z: \operatorname{free}\left(o\right) \to Source, ((\forall x: X, (\operatorname{evaluate}\left(z, \operatorname{theta}\left(o, x\right)\right) = \operatorname{v}\left(x\right))) \land (\forall e: \operatorname{Prod}\left(\operatorname{Term}\left(\operatorname{free}\left(o\right)\right), \operatorname{Term}\left(\operatorname{free}\left(o\right)\right)\right), ((e \in \operatorname{delta}\left(o\right)) \implies (\operatorname{evaluate}\left(z, \operatorname{fst}\left(e\right)\right) \neq \operatorname{evaluate}\left(z, \operatorname{snd}\left(e\right)\right)))))))))))))))))))))$$
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Observer/Constructor/NativeSymbolicRowElimination.complete_row_elimination` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+A raw row is a cut set paired with an arbitrary concrete hole exterior and an arbitrary finite relation on addresses. No attained-row or partition-validity premise is supplied. The compiler fixes the ordered reached list from the source term, rejects relation pairs outside it, and retains every ordered reached pair: membership gives an equation, and nonmembership gives a disequality. This includes diagonals, both orders, repeated class occurrences, every cross-class pair and empty reached sets. The exterior matcher also retains uncut frontier variables and literal address holes.
+
+The finite extra argument contains arbitrary additional free-term equations and disequalities over the same original type. All rows, exterior bindings and extra equations enter one existing native unifier. Its total action reconstructs every original variable, including repeated and unused coordinates. The output explicitly enumerates its free subtype of the original finite presentation. Its domain consists only of arbitrary finite native trees satisfying the substituted disequalities; no positive row equation, shape restriction or normality condition remains. Failure means that no assignment satisfies the positive constraints. Success may still have an empty disequality domain.
+
+For every sufficiently deep prefix pattern, filling the same named frontiers gives the actual original source. The existing symbolic recutting theorem identifies its complete literal row with the symbolic row, preserving the concrete exterior and every partition bit. The second conjunct states that exact actual-source consequence for all prefix-free cuts whose addresses lie above the frontier. Taking the naming map to be the identity gives the original pattern and its literal original frontier tuple.
+
+In the formula, fst and snd are pair projections, free and theta and delta are output fields, and composition(v,name) is the valuation x mapped to v(name(x)). Evaluation after simultaneous substitution reconstructs the same source term because it reconstructs every original coordinate. The result eliminates free row equalities only; equations involving the interpreted substitution history and the general mixed image and cofinality conclusions remain outside its scope.
+

+# Finite Root Fiber Coherence
+
+## Abstract
+
+Under finite positive-degree root fibers, independent roots at every positive degree are equivalent to a genuine monoid homomorphism from Multiplicative Q to H with phi(Multiplicative.ofAdd(1:Q))=h.
+
+**Theorem 1.1 (Under finite positive-degree root fibers, independent roots at every positive degree are equivalent to rational coherence).**
+
+$$\forall H \in Typeu,\; Group\left(H\right) \to \left(\forall h \in H,\; finiteRootFibers\left(H, h\right) \to \left(positiveRootExistence\left(H, h\right) \Leftrightarrow \left(\exists phi \in MonoidHom\left(Multiplicative\left(\mathbb{Q}\right), H\right),\; value\left(phi, ofAdd\left(1\right)\right) = h\right)\right)\right)$$
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/ConceptDynamics/Coding/PrimitiveLifts/FiniteRootFiberCoherence.finite_root_fibers_rational_coherence` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For an arbitrary group H, fix h and assume that every positive-degree fiber {b | b^n=h} is finite. The existence of a root in every positive degree is equivalent to a monoid homomorphism from Multiplicative Q to H with phi(Multiplicative.ofAdd(1:Q))=h. In the formula, ofAdd(q) denotes Multiplicative.ofAdd(q:Q), so ofAdd(1) is additive rational one; the multiplicative identity is ofAdd(0). No commutativity, divisibility, uniqueness, surjectivity, or topology hypothesis is used.
+
+The forward implication is the compactness step. Positive degrees are ordered by divisibility, with common upper bound given by multiplication. The fiber at m maps to the fiber at n for n dividing m by b -> b^(m/n). Mathlib's finite inverse-system section theorem supplies compatible roots without requiring any bonding map to be onto.
+
+For q=a/d define F(q)=b_d^a, with integer exponent. To prove F(q+r)=F(q)F(r), use the single root at d*e*f, where d,e,f are the denominators of q, r, and q+r. Every term is then an integer power of that same group element. Rat.add_num_den' supplies the exponent identity, so no commutation between different group elements is needed. The reverse implication evaluates the homomorphism at Multiplicative.ofAdd(1/n:Q) and uses map_pow.
+
+The theorem asserts existence only. Finite fibers do not imply uniqueness of the resulting homomorphism.
+
+## References
+
+- Truth anchor: `D5/S3/ConceptDynamics/Coding/PrimitiveLifts/FiniteRootFiberCoherence.finite_root_fibers_rational_coherence`

+using static StrataLint.Scribe.DefinitionDsl;

+{
+    private const string Declaration =
+        "D5/S3/ConceptDynamics/Coding/PrimitiveLifts/FiniteRootFiberCoherence."
+            + "finite_root_fibers_rational_coherence";
+

+        "Under finite positive-degree root fibers, independent roots at every positive degree "
+            + "are equivalent to a genuine monoid homomorphism from Multiplicative Q to H "
+            + "with phi(Multiplicative.ofAdd(1:Q))=h.",

+        Blocks(Describe.Lean(
+            DescribeId.Create("finite-root-fibers-rational-coherence"),
+            DeclarationHandle.Create(Declaration),
+            H("Under finite positive-degree root fibers, independent roots at every positive degree "
+                + "are equivalent to rational coherence"),
+            StatementSource.FromAuthor(TheoremFormula()),
+            AssessedProvenance.FromRepo(),
+            Blocks(
+                Paragraph(Text(
+                    "For an arbitrary group H, fix h and assume that every positive-degree "
+                        + "fiber {b | b^n=h} is finite. The existence of a root in every positive "
+                        + "degree is equivalent to a monoid homomorphism from Multiplicative Q to H "
+                        + "with phi(Multiplicative.ofAdd(1:Q))=h. In the formula, ofAdd(q) denotes "
+                        + "Multiplicative.ofAdd(q:Q), so ofAdd(1) is additive rational one; "
+                        + "the multiplicative identity is ofAdd(0). No commutativity, divisibility, uniqueness, "
+                        + "surjectivity, or topology hypothesis is used.")),
+                Paragraph(Text(
+                    "The forward implication is the compactness step. Positive degrees are ordered "
+                        + "by divisibility, with common upper bound given by multiplication. The "
+                        + "fiber at m maps to the fiber at n for n dividing m by b -> b^(m/n). "
+                        + "Mathlib's finite inverse-system section theorem supplies compatible roots "
+                        + "without requiring any bonding map to be onto.")),
+                Paragraph(Text(
+                    "For q=a/d define F(q)=b_d^a, with integer exponent. To prove F(q+r)=F(q)F(r), "
+                        + "use the single root at d*e*f, where d,e,f are the denominators of q, r, "
+                        + "and q+r. Every term is then an integer power of that same group element. "
+                        + "Rat.add_num_den' supplies the exponent identity, so no commutation between "
+                        + "different group elements is needed. The reverse implication evaluates the "
+                        + "homomorphism at Multiplicative.ofAdd(1/n:Q) and uses map_pow.")),
+                Paragraph(Text(
+                    "The theorem asserts existence only. Finite fibers do not imply uniqueness of "
+                        + "the resulting homomorphism."))),
+            DescribeRole.Theorem))));
+
+    private static Formula TheoremFormula()
+    {
+        Formula h = F.Id("h");
+        Formula group = F.Id("H");
+        Formula positiveRoots = Call("positiveRootExistence", group, h);
+        Formula finiteFibers = Call("finiteRootFibers", group, h);
+        Formula rationals = Seq(Mathbb, Grp(F.Id("Q")));
+        Formula actionType = Call("MonoidHom",
+            Call("Multiplicative", rationals), group);
+        Formula phi = F.Id("phi");
+        Formula action = Exists("phi", actionType,
+            Equal(Call("value", phi, Call("ofAdd", D(1))), h));
+        Formula equivalence = new Formula.Logic(
+            positiveRoots, FormulaLogicOperator.Iff, action);
+        Formula hClause = new Formula.TypeArrow(finiteFibers, equivalence);
+        Formula quantifiedH = All("h", group, hClause);
+        Formula groupClause = new Formula.TypeArrow(Call("Group", group), quantifiedH);
+        return Disp(All("H", F.Id("Typeu"), groupClause));
+    }

+    private static Formula Call(string name, params Formula[] arguments) =>
+        new Formula.Apply(F.Id(name), [.. arguments]);
+
+    private static Formula Equal(Formula left, Formula right) =>
+        new Formula.Relation(left, FormulaRelationOperator.Equal, right);
+
+    private static Formula Exists(string name, Formula domain, Formula body) =>
+        new Formula.BindMany(FormulaQuantifier.Exists,
+            [new Formula.BoundVariable(FormulaIdentifier.Create(name), domain)], body);
+
+    private static Formula All(string name, Formula domain, Formula body) =>
+        new Formula.BindMany(FormulaQuantifier.ForAll,
+            [new Formula.BoundVariable(FormulaIdentifier.Create(name), domain)], body);

+# Finite residuals and actual stopping archives
+
+## Abstract
+
+Joint residual signatures preserve actual finite words; stopped execution has exactly the same observational equivalence.
+
+S and Y are arbitrary finite types. K is the existing FiniteMarkovKernel from S to Y times S: every joint row is nonnegative and sums to one. There is one interface, one everywhere legal action, and no failure terminal. K is time homogeneous. No positivity, full support, rationality, determinism or nonemptiness assumption is added. Empty finite types are included wherever such a normalized kernel exists.
+
+Current observation is constant. Thus residual(K,0,x,xp) is True, exactly equality of the current readout. For a relation R, classMass(K,R,x,y,c) sums K(x,(y,r)) over r related to c. The successor residual retains the preceding relation and requires equality of these joint label/class masses for every label and every class representative. Repeated representatives merely repeat the same equation. Each residual is an equivalence relation. This is the decreasing recursive joint-class chain, independently defined from actual word laws.
+
+wordProb(K,x,[]) is one. wordProb(K,x,y::w) sums K(x,(y,r))*wordProb(K,r,w) over all actual successors. TraceEq(K,n,x,xp) means equality of these probabilities for every word of length at most n. Experiment(Y,n) is a finite tree: stop is allowed at any remaining depth; step chooses its continuation solely from the next actual label. Every finite deterministic prefix-dependent stopping policy has this tree representation, and every such tree is allowed. There is no action choice beyond the unique action and no hidden-state test, class test, law-table access, reset, copying or postselection.
+
+**Theorem 1.1 (Soundness at every horizon).**
+
+$$\forall S:Type, (\forall Y:Type, ([\operatorname{Fintype}(S)] [\operatorname{Fintype}(Y)] \forall K:\operatorname{FiniteMarkovKernel}(S,\operatorname{Prod}(Y,S)), (\forall n:Nat, (\forall x:S, (\forall xp:S, (\operatorname{residual}(K,n,x,xp)\Rightarrow\operatorname{TraceEq}(K,n,x,xp)))))))$$
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Observer/ProbabilisticClosure/TrajectoryLaws/FiniteResiduals/FiniteResidualStopping.residual_sound` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Induct on n. At zero only the empty word occurs. For y::w, the induction hypothesis makes r mapped to wordProb(K,r,w) constant on each preceding residual class. Partition the finite successor sum into those classes. Equality of the joint label/class masses makes their weighted sums equal. This grouping is a mathematical integration identity and does not reveal the successor class to the policy.
+
+archiveProb executes the tree chronologically. At stop it gives mass one to the empty suffix. At step its empty suffix has mass zero, and the mass of y::w sums the original joint kernel times the independently executed continuation chosen by y. accepts(E,w) says that w ends at a leaf of this tree, with no earlier stop. Induction on the tree proves archiveProb(K,E,x,w)=wordProb(K,x,w) when accepts(E,w), and zero otherwise. An accepted word has length at most the depth. This proves the word/archive correspondence rather than identifying the two laws by definition.
+
+**Theorem 1.2 (Exact operational stopping characterization).**
+
+$$\forall S:Type, (\forall Y:Type, ([\operatorname{Fintype}(S)] [\operatorname{Fintype}(Y)] \forall K:\operatorname{FiniteMarkovKernel}(S,\operatorname{Prod}(Y,S)), (\forall n:Nat, (\forall x:S, (\forall xp:S, (\operatorname{TraceEq}(K,n,x,xp)\Leftrightarrow\operatorname{StoppingEq}(K,n,x,xp)))))))$$
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Observer/ProbabilisticClosure/TrajectoryLaws/FiniteResiduals/FiniteResidualStopping.trace_iff_stopping` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+StoppingEq quantifies over every k at most n, every Experiment(Y,k), and every complete archive word. For the forward direction, use the independently proved accepted-prefix formula and its length bound. For the reverse direction, use the legal tree that continues exactly length(w) steps and then stops. These arguments include immediate stopping, the empty word, horizon zero and branches of zero probability. A suffix discarded by stopping is summed out; no observer operation on that suffix is introduced.
+
+**Theorem 1.3 (The executed archives are probability laws).**
+
+$$\forall S:Type, (\forall Y:Type, ([\operatorname{Fintype}(S)] [\operatorname{Fintype}(Y)] \forall K:\operatorname{FiniteMarkovKernel}(S,\operatorname{Prod}(Y,S)), (\forall n:Nat, (\forall E:\operatorname{Experiment}(Y,n), (\forall x:S, ((\forall w:\operatorname{List}(Y), (0\leq\operatorname{archiveProb}(K,E,x,w)))\land (\forall w:\operatorname{List}(Y), (n<\operatorname{length}(w)\Rightarrow\operatorname{archiveProb}(K,E,x,w)=0))\land \sum_{w\in \operatorname{leaves}(E)}\operatorname{archiveProb}(K,E,x,w)=1))))))$$
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Observer/ProbabilisticClosure/TrajectoryLaws/FiniteResiduals/FiniteResidualStopping.archive_probability_law` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+leaves(E) is the finite set of complete archive words at which E stops. The first conjunct is pointwise nonnegativity, the second excludes words longer than n, and the last sums the archive probabilities over leaves(E). For step, the prefix sets y::leaves(E(y)) are pairwise disjoint. Their total mass is the sum over y and r of K(x,(y,r)) times the continuation mass one. Row normalization gives one. At stop, the sole leaf is the empty word.
+
+If a constant c is recorded only initially, the complete record is (c,w), with inverse given by the word projection. If it is recorded initially and at every node, the record is (c,map(y mapped to (y,c),w)), again with inverse given by projecting the labels. Both encodings are injective on actual archives, including the empty archive, and pushing any of the finite laws through them preserves and reflects equality. Prefix decisions pull back through these same encodings, so neither convention supplies additional control. This is a finite single-action result; it makes no unrestricted stochastic decoder or semantic-factorization assertion.
+
+## References

+# Six-state separation of archives and joint residuals
+
+## Abstract
+
+The same normalized six-state process has identical stopping archives, distinct permanent residuals, and no almost-sure label update.
+
+The states s,t,u,v,w,z are Fin(6) indices 0,1,2,3,4,5, and labels 0,1 are false,true. The complete nonzero joint kernel is: s to (0,u) and (0,v), each one half; t to (0,w), mass one; u to (0,z), mass one; v to (1,z), mass one; w to (0,z) and (1,z), each one half; z to (0,z), mass one. Every omitted entry is zero. The rows are nonnegative and normalized. The ordinary absorbing state z can continue forever. All current observations are constant, the unique action is everywhere legal, and there is no failure or extra control.
+
+The original recursive residual is used throughout. firstClass has fibers {s,t,u,z}, {v}, {w}, and equality of firstClass is exactly residual(K,1). stableClass has fibers {s}, {t}, {u,z}, {v}, {w}, and equality of stableClass is exactly residual(K,2). The six signatures using the first-stage classes are: s gives half (0,Czero) plus half (0,Cone); t gives (0,Chalf); u and z give (0,Czero); v gives (1,Czero); w gives half (0,Czero) plus half (1,Czero). Hence s and t agree at the first stage and differ at the second. The only nonsingleton second-stage fiber is {u,z}; both rows send mass one to (0,{u,z}). The next refinement equals the second, and induction gives residual(K,n+2)=residual(K,2) for every n. Its intersection over all horizons is exactly stableClass equality.
+
+For z, an all-zero word has mass one and every other word mass zero, by induction on word length. From s and t the empty word and one-letter word 0 have mass one; the one-letter word 1 has mass zero. A word of length at least two has mass one half exactly when its first letter is 0 and every letter after its second is 0. Thus 00 and 01 each have mass one half, and each may be followed only by zeroes. This computes the same all-depth profile from the same kernel at both initial states. The operational characterization gives equality of every allowed stopping law at every finite horizon, although the second and limiting residuals separate s and t.
+
+representative selects s,t,u,v,w for the five stableClass values. quotientRow(q,(y,d)) sums the original row from representative(q) over successors with stableClass d. The proof checks that every original representative x gives exactly quotientRow(stableClass(x),(y,d)); the only distinct representatives of one fiber are u,z. Summing over y and d gives one, and all entries are nonnegative. StochasticQuotient includes both this normalized joint kernel and the exact identification of stableClass fibers with the original limiting residual. This is a stochastic quotient of the same process, not a separately selected model.
+
+For any proposed deterministic update, updateFailure(update,x) is the sum of the actual original joint masses of branches whose successor class differs from update(stableClass(x),label). From s the two successful branches (0,u) and (0,v) each have mass one half and distinct successor classes. One predicted class cannot equal both; consequently updateFailure(update,s) is at least one half. In particular it cannot be zero, which rules out the update even almost surely. Zero-mass branches are retained in the sum and contribute zero.
+
+claim is the disjunction of two assertions about this one process. The first says that for every pair of states, equality of every finite stopping experiment at every horizon entails equality of the recursive residuals at every horizon. The second says that StochasticQuotient entails existence of a deterministic update with updateFailure zero at every state. Refuting this disjunction refutes each assertion separately: the first uses the all-depth stopping premise at s,t and their actual second-stage separation; the second uses the actual normalized stochastic quotient and the positive update-failure bound.
+
+**Theorem 1.1 (Complete same-kernel correction).**
+
+$$(\forall x:\operatorname{Fin}(6), (\forall xp:\operatorname{Fin}(6), (\operatorname{residual}(kernel,1,x,xp)\Leftrightarrow\operatorname{firstClass}(x)=\operatorname{firstClass}(xp))))\land (\forall x:\operatorname{Fin}(6), (\forall xp:\operatorname{Fin}(6), (\operatorname{residual}(kernel,2,x,xp)\Leftrightarrow\operatorname{stableClass}(x)=\operatorname{stableClass}(xp))))\land (\forall n:Nat, (\operatorname{residual}(kernel,n+2)=\operatorname{residual}(kernel,2)))\land (\forall x:\operatorname{Fin}(6), (\forall xp:\operatorname{Fin}(6), ((\forall n:Nat, (\operatorname{residual}(kernel,n,x,xp)))\Leftrightarrow\operatorname{stableClass}(x)=\operatorname{stableClass}(xp))))\land (\forall w:\operatorname{List}(Bool), (\operatorname{wordProb}(kernel,0,w)=\operatorname{profile}(w)\land \operatorname{wordProb}(kernel,1,w)=\operatorname{profile}(w)))\land (\forall n:Nat, (\operatorname{StoppingEq}(kernel,n,0,1)))\land (\operatorname{residual}(kernel,1,0,1))\land (\neg \operatorname{residual}(kernel,2,0,1))\land (\neg (\forall n:Nat, (\operatorname{residual}(kernel,n,0,1))))\land (StochasticQuotient)\land (\forall update:\operatorname{Fin}(5)\Rightarrow Bool\Rightarrow \operatorname{Fin}(5), (\frac{1}{2}\leq\operatorname{updateFailure}(update,0)))$$
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Observer/ProbabilisticClosure/TrajectoryLaws/FiniteResiduals/SixStateResidualSeparation.counterkernel_facts` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+The conjunction gives both complete finite partitions, the permanent plateau and its limiting partition, the actual all-depth word profile and stopping equality, the first-stage agreement and second-stage and limiting separation, the normalized stochastic quotient, and the positive update-failure bound. Every occurrence of kernel denotes the single joint kernel specified above.
+
+**Theorem 1.2 (Both withdrawn implications fail on the same kernel).**
+
+$$\neg claim$$
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Observer/ProbabilisticClosure/TrajectoryLaws/FiniteResiduals/SixStateResidualSeparation.result` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+The two cases of the disjunction are contradicted independently. The archive comparison uses the all-depth common word profile and the exact stopping theorem. The quotient comparison uses its representative independence and normalization before the update obstruction. Thus the random successor-class distribution is well defined, while the current class and observed label do not determine the realized successor class.
+
+The valid implication from recursive residuals to finite archive laws remains. Equality of actual archive laws does not in general identify the recursive quotient or its claimed minimality, and it does not justify merging states in that quotient. No general stochastic factorization or decoder repair is asserted. A common decoder still pushes equal archive laws to equal response laws; identifying those responses with a semantic residual requires a separate characterization. Recursive sufficient-boundary claims must also preserve current observations. The example specifies no semantic event kernel, semantic residual or decoder, so it does not settle theorems under additional such hypotheses. Permission-delay, graft and coordinate-recovery claims retain their own menu, readout, successor and inverse-map conditions. None is proved or refuted here by association, and no physical or empirical consequence follows.

+        return And(a,b,c,d,e,f,g,h,i,j,l);
+    }
+    private static Formula And(params Formula[] xs)
+    {
+        var parts = new Formula[xs.Length * 4 - 1];
+        for (var i = 0; i < xs.Length; i++)
+        {
+            var z = 4 * i;
+            parts[z] = Open; parts[z+1] = xs[i]; parts[z+2] = Close;
+            if (i < xs.Length - 1) parts[z+3] = F.Seq(Land, Sp);
+        }
+        return Seq(parts);
+    }
+    private static Formula All(string name, Formula type, Formula body) =>
+        Seq(Forall, Sp, F.Id(name), Colon, type, Comma, Sp, Open, body, Close);
+    private static Formula Fraction(Formula a, Formula b) => Seq(Frac, Grp(a), Grp(b));
+    private static Formula Seq(params Formula[] xs) => F.Seq(xs);
+    private static Formula Call(string name, params Formula[] xs)
+    {
+        var parts = new Formula[xs.Length * 2 - 1];
+        for (var i = 0; i < xs.Length; i++) { parts[2*i] = xs[i]; if (i > 0) parts[2*i-1] = Comma; }
+        return Seq(Operatorname, Grp(F.Id(name)), Open, Seq(parts), Close);
+    }

+def IsSourceSeries (A : PowerSeries ℤ) : Prop :=
+  PowerSeries.constantCoeff A = 1 ∧
+    ∀ m : ℕ, 0 < m →
+      (Finset.range m).sum (fun j : ℕ => PowerSeries.coeff j
+        ((PowerSeries.rescale (((m : ℚ)⁻¹))
+          (A.map (Int.castRingHom ℚ))) ^ m)) = (4 : ℚ) ^ (m - 1)
+
+def claim : Prop :=
+  (∃ A : PowerSeries ℤ, IsSourceSeries A) ∧
+    ∀ A : PowerSeries ℤ, IsSourceSeries A →
+      ∀ n : ℕ, 3 < n →
+        (Odd (PowerSeries.coeff n A) ↔
+          ∃ k : ℕ, 1 < k ∧ (n = 2 ^ k - 1 ∨ n = 2 ^ k + 1))
+
+theorem result : D5.S1.Recurrence.LinearRows.QuadrupledLinearExponentDyadicSupport.claim := by
+  classical
+  change (∃ A : PowerSeries ℤ, IsSourceSeries A) ∧
+    ∀ A : PowerSeries ℤ, IsSourceSeries A →
+      ∀ n : ℕ, 3 < n →
+        (Odd (PowerSeries.coeff n A) ↔
+          ∃ k : ℕ, 1 < k ∧ (n = 2 ^ k - 1 ∨ n = 2 ^ k + 1))
+  -- First clear the NAME denominators, retaining all positive rows.
+  have hscale (A : PowerSeries Int) (n : Nat) :
+      ((n + 1 : Nat) : Rat)^n *
+        (Finset.range (n+1)).sum (fun j => coeff j
+          ((rescale (((n+1 : Nat) : Rat)⁻¹)
+            (A.map (Int.castRingHom Rat)))^(n+1))) = ((row A n : Int) : Rat) := by
+    have hm : ((n+1 : Nat) : Rat) ≠ 0 :=
+      Nat.cast_ne_zero.mpr (Nat.succ_ne_zero n)
+    have hmap : row (A.map (Int.castRingHom Rat)) n = ((row A n : Int) : Rat) := by
+      simp only [row, ← geom_map (Int.castRingHom Rat), ← map_pow, ← map_mul, coeff_map]
+      rfl
+    rw [← hmap, row, coeff_mul, Finset.Nat.sum_antidiagonal_eq_sum_range_succ_mk]
+    simp only [← map_pow, coeff_rescale, geom, coeff_mk, Finset.mul_sum]
+    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+    intro j hj
+    have hjn : j ≤ n := Finset.mem_range_succ_iff.mp hj
+    rw [pow_sub₀ _ hm hjn, inv_pow]
+    ring
+  -- This is the complete equivalence with the source's formula (2), using its
+  -- constant-one formal inverse, rather than an assumed alternative source.
+  have hname_row (A : PowerSeries Int) : IsSourceSeries A ↔
+      constantCoeff A = 1 ∧ ∀ m : Nat, 0 < m →
+        coeff (m-1) (A^m * invOfUnit (1-C (m : Int)*X) 1) =
+          (4 * (m : Int))^(m-1) := by
+    have hr (n : Nat) : row A n =
+        coeff n (A^(n+1) * invOfUnit (1-C ((n+1 : Nat) : Int)*X) 1) := by
+      rw [row, geom_inverse]
+    constructor
+    · rintro ⟨h0, hA⟩
+      refine ⟨h0, ?_⟩
+      intro m hm
+      obtain ⟨n, rfl⟩ := Nat.exists_eq_succ_of_ne_zero (Nat.ne_of_gt hm)
+      have h := hscale A n
+      rw [hA (n+1) (by omega), Nat.add_sub_cancel] at h
+      have h' : row A n = (4 * ((n+1 : Nat) : Int))^n := by
+        apply Int.cast_injective (α := Rat)
+        push_cast
+        rw [← h, mul_pow]
+        push_cast
+        ring
+      simpa only [Nat.succ_eq_add_one, Nat.add_sub_cancel, hr] using h'
+    · rintro ⟨h0, hA⟩
+      refine ⟨h0, ?_⟩
+      intro m hm
+      obtain ⟨n, rfl⟩ := Nat.exists_eq_succ_of_ne_zero (Nat.ne_of_gt hm)
+      have h := hscale A n
+      have ha := hA (n+1) (by omega)
+      simp only [Nat.add_sub_cancel] at ha
+      rw [hr, ha] at h
+      have hm' : (((n+1 : Nat) : Rat)^n) ≠ 0 :=
+        pow_ne_zero _ (Nat.cast_ne_zero.mpr (Nat.succ_ne_zero n))
+      apply (mul_left_cancel₀ hm')
+      simpa only [Nat.succ_eq_add_one, Nat.add_sub_cancel, Int.cast_pow,
+        Int.cast_mul, Int.cast_ofNat, Int.cast_natCast, mul_pow, mul_comm] using h
+  let t : Nat → Int := fun n => 4^n * ((n+1 : Nat) : Int)^(n-1)
+  have hfactor (n : Nat) (hn : 0 < n) :
+      (4 * ((n+1 : Nat) : Int))^n = ((n+1 : Nat) : Int) * t n := by
+    dsimp [t]
+    have hp : ((n+1 : Nat) : Int)^n = ((n+1 : Nat) : Int) * ((n+1 : Nat) : Int)^(n-1) := by
+      rw [← pow_succ', Nat.sub_add_cancel hn]
+    simp only [Nat.cast_add, Nat.cast_one] at hp
+    rw [mul_pow, hp]
+    ring
+  have hnormalized (A : PowerSeries Int) : IsSourceSeries A ↔
+      constantCoeff A = 1 ∧ ∀ n : Nat, 0 < n → normalized A n = t n := by
+    rw [hname_row]
+    constructor
+    · rintro ⟨h0, hA⟩
+      refine ⟨h0, ?_⟩
+      intro n hn
+      have h := hA (n+1) (by omega)
+      rw [← geom_inverse, Nat.add_sub_cancel] at h
+      change row A n = _ at h
+      rw [exact_normalization A n hn, hfactor n hn] at h
+      exact mul_left_cancel₀ (by positivity : ((n+1 : Nat) : Int) ≠ 0) h
+    · rintro ⟨h0, hA⟩
+      refine ⟨h0, ?_⟩
+      intro m hm
+      obtain ⟨n, rfl⟩ := Nat.exists_eq_succ_of_ne_zero (Nat.ne_of_gt hm)
+      cases n with
+      | zero => simpa using h0
+      | succ n =>
+        rw [← geom_inverse]
+        change row A (n+1) = (4 * ((n+1+1 : Nat) : Int))^(n+1)
+        rw [exact_normalization A (n+1) (by omega), hA (n+1) (by omega),
+          hfactor (n+1) (by omega)]
+  -- Integer iteration: the forcing term is added after the existing advance.
+  let forcing : PowerSeries Int := mk fun n => if n=0 then 0 else t n
+  let step : PowerSeries Int → PowerSeries Int := fun F => advance F + forcing
+  have step_zero (F : PowerSeries Int) : constantCoeff (step F) = 1 := by
+    simp [step, forcing, advance_zero]
+  have step_agree {d : Nat} {F G : PowerSeries Int}
+      (hF : constantCoeff F = 1) (hG : constantCoeff G = 1) (h : Agree d F G) :
+      Agree (d+1) (step F) (step G) := by
+    intro k hk
+    simpa only [step, map_add] using
+      congrArg (fun z : Int => z + coeff k forcing) (advance_agree hF hG h k hk)
+  obtain ⟨A, A_zero, A_fixed, _⟩ :=
+    D5.S1.Recurrence.Invariants.PowerSeriesNormalizedContraction.exists_unique_fixed
+      step (fun F _ => step_zero F)
+      (fun _ hF hG h => step_agree hF hG h)
+  have A_normalized (n : Nat) (hn : 0 < n) : normalized A n = t n := by
+    have h := congrArg (coeff n) A_fixed
+    simp only [step, map_add, advance, forcing, coeff_mk, if_neg (by omega : n ≠ 0)] at h
+    linear_combination h
+  have A_source : IsSourceSeries A := (hnormalized A).mpr ⟨A_zero, A_normalized⟩
+  refine ⟨⟨A, A_source⟩, ?_⟩
+  intro B hB n hn
+  obtain ⟨B_zero, B_normalized⟩ := (hnormalized B).mp hB
+  -- Reduction takes place only after normalization over the integers.
+  have hmod : B.map (Int.castRingHom (ZMod 2)) =
+      (solution (R := Int)).map (Int.castRingHom (ZMod 2)) := by
+    apply normalized_unique
+    · rw [← coeff_zero_eq_constantCoeff, coeff_map, coeff_zero_eq_constantCoeff, B_zero, map_one]
+    · rw [← coeff_zero_eq_constantCoeff, coeff_map, coeff_zero_eq_constantCoeff,
+        solution_zero, map_one]
+    · intro j hj
+      rw [normalized_map, B_normalized j hj]
+      have ht : (Int.castRingHom (ZMod 2)) (t j) = 0 := by
+        have hj0 : j ≠ 0 := Nat.ne_of_gt hj
+        simp only [t, map_mul, map_pow]
+        have h4 : (Int.castRingHom (ZMod 2)) (4 : Int) = 0 :=
+          (ZMod.val_eq_zero ((Int.castRingHom (ZMod 2)) 4)).mp rfl
+        rw [h4, zero_pow hj0, zero_mul]
+      exact ht
+    · intro j hj
+      rw [normalized_map, solution_normalized j hj, map_zero]
+  have hc : ((coeff n B : Int) : ZMod 2) = ((coeff n generatingSeries : Int) : ZMod 2) := by
+    have h := congrArg (coeff n) hmod
+    simpa only [coeff_map, Int.coe_castRingHom, generatingSeries, map_sub, coeff_one,
+      if_neg (by omega : n ≠ 0), zero_sub, Int.cast_neg, CharTwo.neg_eq] using h
+  rw [← ZMod.intCast_eq_one_iff_odd, hc, ZMod.intCast_eq_one_iff_odd]
+  exact hanna_conjecture generatingSeries generating_equation n hn
+
+end D5.S1.Recurrence.LinearRows.QuadrupledLinearExponentDyadicSupport

+/-- Replace precisely the encountered cut subtrees by the native leaf alpha. -/
+def nativeMask (Q : CutSet) : Address → Source → Source
+  | a, .of b => if a ∈ Q then .of true else .of b
+  | a, .mul l r => if a ∈ Q then .of true else
+      .mul (nativeMask Q (a ++ [false]) l) (nativeMask Q (a ++ [true]) r)
+
+/-- Fill every literal address hole by alpha, retaining all concrete leaves. -/
+def fillMask : HoleExterior →ₙ* Source :=
+  FreeMagma.lift (Sum.elim FreeMagma.of (fun _ => .of true))
+
+/-- The mask expression keeps every uncut frontier variable literally. -/
+def maskExpression {X : Type} : SymbolicExterior X →ₙ* Term X :=
+  FreeMagma.lift (Sum.elim FreeMagma.of (fun _ => .of (.inl true)))
+
+private theorem mask_expression_fill {X : Type} (v : X → Source)
+    (e : SymbolicExterior X) :
+    evaluate v (maskExpression e) = fillMask (exteriorFill v e) := by
+  have embedded : fillMask.comp (FreeMagma.map Sum.inl) = MulHom.id Source := by
+    apply FreeMagma.hom_ext
+    funext b
+    rfl
+  have h : (evaluate v).comp maskExpression = fillMask.comp (exteriorFill v) := by
+    apply FreeMagma.hom_ext
+    funext a
+    cases a with
+    | inl b => cases b with
+      | inl b => rfl
+      | inr x =>
+          change v x = fillMask (FreeMagma.map Sum.inl (v x))
+          exact (congrArg (fun f : Source →ₙ* Source => f (v x)) embedded).symm
+    | inr q => rfl
+  exact congrArg (fun f : SymbolicExterior X →ₙ* Source => f e) h
+
+private theorem mask_fill (Q : CutSet) (a : Address) (u : Source) :
+    nativeMask Q a u = fillMask (cutExterior Q a u) := by
+  induction u generalizing a with
+  | of b => by_cases h : a ∈ Q <;> simp [nativeMask, cutExterior, fillMask, h]
+  | mul l r ihl ihr =>
+      by_cases h : a ∈ Q
+      · simp [nativeMask, cutExterior, fillMask, h]
+      · simp only [nativeMask, cutExterior, h, ↓reduceIte, FreeMagma.mul_eq, map_mul]
+        exact congrArg₂ (· * ·) (ihl _) (ihr _)
+
+/-- Replacing the same cuts in the mask recovers every original exterior node. -/
+private theorem mask_restore (Q : CutSet) (a : Address) (u : Source) :
+    cutExterior Q a (nativeMask Q a u) = cutExterior Q a u := by
+  induction u generalizing a with
+  | of b => by_cases h : a ∈ Q <;> simp [nativeMask, cutExterior, h]
+  | mul l r ihl ihr =>
+      by_cases h : a ∈ Q
+      · simp [nativeMask, cutExterior, h]
+      · simp only [nativeMask, cutExterior, h, ↓reduceIte]
+        exact congrArg₂ FreeMagma.mul (ihl _) (ihr _)
+
+/-- Raw exteriors also have to put their literal address holes at their cuts.
+This is a computed check, rather than an attained-label certificate. -/
+private theorem mask_exterior_exact (Q : CutSet) (u : Source) (e : HoleExterior) :
+    cutExterior Q [] u = e ↔
+      cutExterior Q [] (fillMask e) = e ∧
+      nativeMask Q [] u = fillMask e ∧
+      (reachedHoles Q [] u).toFinset = (exteriorHoles [] e).toFinset := by
+  constructor
+  · intro h
+    subst e
+    refine ⟨?_, mask_fill Q [] u, ?_⟩
+    · rw [← mask_fill, mask_restore]
+    · rw [ActualCutPartitionDecoder.exteriorHoles_cut]
+  · rintro ⟨coherent, mask, _⟩
+    exact (mask_restore Q [] u).symm.trans
+      ((congrArg (cutExterior Q []) mask).trans coherent)
+
+private theorem mask_sources_exact (Q : CutSet) (u w : Source) :
+    (nativeMask Q [] u = nativeMask Q [] w ∧
+      (reachedHoles Q [] u).toFinset = (reachedHoles Q [] w).toFinset) ↔
+      cutExterior Q [] u = cutExterior Q [] w := by
+  rw [mask_exterior_exact]
+  have coherent : cutExterior Q [] (fillMask (cutExterior Q [] w)) = cutExterior Q [] w := by
+    rw [← mask_fill, mask_restore]
+  rw [coherent, ← mask_fill, ActualCutPartitionDecoder.exteriorHoles_cut]
+  simp only [true_and]
+
+/-- Both complete exterior descriptors and the entire reached-pair relation.
+The coherence conjunct rejects malformed raw address labels. -/
+def maskRowHolds (r : RawRow) (u : Source) : Prop :=
+  (cutExterior r.1 [] (fillMask r.2.1) = r.2.1 ∧
+    nativeMask r.1 [] u = fillMask r.2.1 ∧
+    (reachedHoles r.1 [] u).toFinset = (exteriorHoles [] r.2.1).toFinset) ∧
+    actualPartition r.1 u = r.2.2
+
+private theorem mask_row_exact (r : RawRow) (u : Source) :
+    maskRowHolds r u ↔ literalRecord r.1 u = r.2 := by
+  rcases r with ⟨Q, e, K⟩
+  rw [maskRowHolds, ← mask_exterior_exact]
+  simp only [literalRecord, Prod.mk.injEq]
+
+/-- Mask and reached-set equality characterize complete original exteriors.
+Every row of the same filled original pattern is then eliminated together,
+with one unrestricted family reconstructing all original coordinates. -/
+theorem original_mask_row_elimination {X : Type} (p : Presentation X)
+    (d : Nat) (pat : NativeDepthPatterns.Pattern d)
+    (name : NativeDepthPatterns.Frontier pat → X)
+    (rs : List RawRow) (extra : SignedConstraints X) (v : X → Source)
+    (freecuts : ∀ r ∈ rs, CutPrefixFree r.1)
+    (bound : ∀ r ∈ rs, ∀ q ∈ r.1, q.length < d) :
+    (∀ (Q : CutSet) (u w : Source),
+      (nativeMask Q [] u = nativeMask Q [] w ∧
+        (reachedHoles Q [] u).toFinset = (reachedHoles Q [] w).toFinset) ↔
+        cutExterior Q [] u = cutExterior Q [] w) ∧
+    (∀ r ∈ rs,
+      evaluate v (maskExpression (symbolicExterior r.1 []
+        (NativeHistoryCells.patternTerm pat name))) =
+        nativeMask r.1 [] (NativeDepthPatterns.fill pat (v ∘ name))) ∧
+    (((∀ r ∈ rs, maskRowHolds r (NativeDepthPatterns.fill pat (v ∘ name))) ∧
+      constraintsHold extra v) ↔
+      ∃ o, eliminateRows p (NativeHistoryCells.patternTerm pat name) rs extra = some o ∧
+        outputHolds o v) := by
+  refine ⟨mask_sources_exact, ?_, ?_⟩
+  · intro r hr
+    rw [mask_expression_fill]
+    have deep := NativeHistoryCells.pattern_deep d d pat name [] (by simp)
+    have he := (NativeSymbolicRecutting.symbolic_recut_exact d r.1
+      (freecuts r hr) (bound r hr) (NativeHistoryCells.patternTerm pat name) deep v).2.1
+    rw [← he, ← mask_fill, NativeHistoryCells.pattern_evaluate]
+  · have rows :
+        (∀ r ∈ rs, maskRowHolds r (NativeDepthPatterns.fill pat (v ∘ name))) ↔
+        (∀ r ∈ rs, literalRecord r.1 (NativeDepthPatterns.fill pat (v ∘ name)) = r.2) := by
+      constructor <;> intro h r hr
+      · exact (mask_row_exact r _).mp (h r hr)
+      · exact (mask_row_exact r _).mpr (h r hr)
+    exact (and_congr rows Iff.rfl).trans
+      ((complete_row_elimination p (NativeHistoryCells.patternTerm pat name) rs extra v).2
+        d pat name rfl freecuts bound)
+
+end D5.S3.Arith.FibonacciAtomic.Observer.Constructor.NativeMaskRowElimination

+namespace D5.S3.Arith.FibonacciAtomic.Observer.Constructor.NativeSymbolicRowElimination

+open GenealogicalFiberTransport (Source)
+open NativeGroundSeparation (Term evaluate)
+open NativeSymbolicRecutting (SymbolicExterior exteriorFill)
+open ActualCutPartitionDecoder (HoleExterior)
